mutants.change: the producer ignores the queue bound C
a failed attempt goes back on the bounded queue instead of staying with its sender
the count and the ack are two steps, so a redelivered message counts twice
the take is a read and then a pop, so two senders can take one message

attempts.doc: A: attempts per message, at most

backoff_us.doc: beta: wait beta 2^(j-1) before attempt j, us

fail_ppm.doc: p: failure probability per attempt, ppm

rate.doc: lambda: arrivals per second, 0 = all at once

seed.doc: s: every random choice derives from it

workers.doc: P: processes or pods, each with M senders

properties.claim: Every message has 0 <= length <= 100 symbols from the alphabet and is a pure function of (seed, i).

For any queue (threads, processes or a stream), any senders started and stopped during the run, a sender killed holding a message, and any interleaving, the committed total equals the pure fold run_range(0, N); a redelivered message counts once.
At most C messages are queued and at most P M are in flight; the producer blocks at C, so the heap is O(C + M), independent of N.
Over 2^16 messages, failure rates lie within Bernstein bounds of p and p^A and the mean latency within a Chernoff bound of mu, at delta = 1e-9; p = 0 and p = 1 are exact.
For the closed batch (lambda = 0), in virtual time the makespan T obeys max(S/M, max tau) <= T <= S/M + (1 - 1/M) max tau (Graham); in the model every reachable state drains.
The monitor sums each sender's latest report. Its snapshots never decrease, in virtual time each follows the previous one by T (the last by at most T), and the last equals the committed total.

With Poisson arrivals at lambda below the capacity M / E[tau], the rates in and out are within 15% of lambda; at 4x the capacity the queue fills to C and the rate in falls to the rate out, within 15% of the capacity.
